questions.question: Thomas went for a run. He stopped to check his pulse and counted 39 beats in 15 seconds. How can Thomas calculate his pulse rate in beats per minute?
questions.answer: The rate per second is $39 \div 15$; there are $60$ seconds in a minute, so multiply by $60$: $39 \div 15 \times 60 = 156$ beats per minute. **(C)**

questions.question: A survey asked students to indicate their favourite pet from the list: dog, cat, fish, bird, rabbit, or other. What type of data is this?
questions.answer: The responses are categories with no natural order, so the data is categorical nominal. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a linear function?
questions.answer: $y = -\dfrac{3}{x}$ is a reciprocal (inverse variation) function, whose graph is a hyperbola. The others have the form $y = mx + c$. **(C)**

questions.question: As of 2025, the current official land speed record is held by ThrustSSC at a speed of almost 1228 km/h. What is this speed in metres per second?
A laptop costs \$899, including 10% GST. What is the price of the laptop before GST?
questions.answer: The price including GST is $110\%$ of the original price: $\dfrac{899}{1.1} = \$817.27$. **(C)**
The trains arriving at Gadigal before 8:30 are the ones reaching it at 08:15 and 08:25. The latest of these arrives at Gadigal at 08:25 and leaves Cherrybrook at 07:54. **(D)**

questions.question: Charlie invested \$22 000 that will be compounded monthly at 6% per annum. Which calculation will give the value of his investment after four years?
questions.answer: The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12} = 0.5\%$ and the number of compounding periods is $4 \times 12 = 48$. So $FV = 22\,000\left(1 + \dfrac{0.5}{100}\right)^{48}$. **(B)**

questions.question: Daniel has 1000 shares in Alphabet Corp. A dividend of 18 cents per share is paid on his shares with a market value per share of \$4.50. What is the dividend yield?
questions.answer: Dividend yield $= \dfrac{0.18}{4.50} \times 100 = 4\%$. **(D)**

questions.question: Siem Reap has a latitude of $13^\circ$ N and a longitude of $104^\circ$ E. Bangkok is due west of Siem Reap. The coordinates of Bangkok could be:
questions.answer: Due west means the same latitude ($13^\circ$ N) and a smaller longitude east of Greenwich. Only $(13^\circ\text{ N}, 100^\circ\text{ E})$ fits. **(B)**

questions.question: Tom's normal rate of pay is \$26.40 per hour. In one week, he worked 16 hours at the normal rate, 5.5 hours at time-and-a-half, and 3 hours at double time. He also received a danger allowance of \$72 for the week. What were his total earnings for the week?
The Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) of Sydney, Australia is $+10$ hours and the UTC of Toronto, Canada is $-4$ hours. What is the local time in Toronto if it is 8 am on Monday in Sydney?
questions.answer: Toronto is $10 - (-4) = 14$ hours behind Sydney. $8$ am Monday $- 14$ h $= 6$ pm Sunday. **(B)**

questions.question: Jonah is asked to solve $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{4x}{3} + 3$. Which of the following could be Jonah's next step?
questions.answer: Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator, $6$: $3(x - 1) = 2(4x) + 18$. **(C)**

questions.question: Ten students sat a practice trial examination and received the following marks: 67, 92, 68, 88, 87, 79, 91, 76, 82, 90. After further revision, the examination was repeated and each student's mark increased by 7. When comparing the second set of results with the first:
questions.answer: Adding a constant to every value shifts the mean by that constant but does not change the spread, so the mean increases by $7$ and the standard deviation stays the same. **(B)**
options: the mean had decreased by 7 and the standard deviation had remained the same.
the mean had increased by 7 and the standard deviation had remained the same.
the mean had decreased by 7 and the standard deviation had increased by 7.
the mean had increased by 7 and the standard deviation had increased by 7.

questions.question: A mountain bike course is represented by a network of tracks, where each track is modelled as an edge connecting two vertices. Due to bad weather, two tracks have been closed. After these closures, Thomas is able to cycle a route that uses each remaining track exactly once without repetition. He may start and finish at different locations. Which one of the following options does NOT allow such a route to be completed?
questions.answer:
A route using every edge exactly once exists only if the network has $0$ or $2$ vertices of odd degree. The degrees are $A = 4$, $B = 2$, $C = 3$, $D = 5$, $E = 4$, $F = 2$, $G = 4$.

- (A) $AG$, $CG$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $C = 2$, so the odd vertices are $A$ and $D$.
- (B) $AG$, $DG$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $D = 4$, so the odd vertices are $A$ and $C$.
- (C) $AG$, $GE$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $E = 3$, so the odd vertices are $A$, $C$, $D$, $E$ (four odd vertices).
- (D) $CE$, $DG$ closed: $C = 2$, $E = 3$, $D = 4$, $G = 3$, so the odd vertices are $E$ and $G$.

Only (C) has four odd vertices. **(C)**

questions.question: The area of a trapezium has the formula $A = \dfrac{h}{2}(a + b)$. Make $b$ the subject of the formula.
questions.answer: $$2A = h(a + b) \Rightarrow \frac{2A}{h} = a + b \Rightarrow b = \frac{2A}{h} - a$$

questions.question: A school purchases a photocopier for \$12 000. It depreciates at a rate of 15% per annum, using the declining balance method. Calculate the value of the photocopier after 4 years.

Cohen is taking out a loan of \$60 000 at an interest rate of 8.41% per annum. The interest is calculated monthly on a reducible basis. The table shows the progress of the first three months of the loan.

| Month | Principal | Interest | Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | \$60 000.00 | \$420.50 | \$59 473.02 |
| 2 | \$59 473.02 | \$416.81 | \$58 942.35 |
| 3 | \$58 942.35 | \$413.09 | \$58 407.96 |
| 4 | \$58 407.96 | $A$ | $B$ |

What is the regular monthly repayment?
questions.answer: Repayment $=$ principal $+$ interest $-$ balance $= 60\,000 + 420.50 - 59\,473.02 = \$947.48$.

questions.question: Cohen's loan of \$60 000 has an interest rate of 8.41% per annum, calculated monthly on a reducible basis, with a monthly repayment of \$947.48. In month 4 the principal is \$58 407.96, the interest is $A$ and the balance is $B$. Calculate the values of $A$ and $B$.
Cohen's loan of \$60 000 requires monthly repayments of \$947.48 and will be paid off after 84 months. How much interest will Cohen pay in this time?

A fruit punch is made by mixing orange juice, apple juice, and pineapple juice in the ratio $3 : 4 : 5$. Angus wants to make 96 litres of this fruit punch for his party. How many litres of each type of juice should he use?
questions.answer:
Total parts $= 3 + 4 + 5 = 12$, so each part is $96 \div 12 = 8$ L.

Orange: $3 \times 8 = 24$ L; apple: $4 \times 8 = 32$ L; pineapple: $5 \times 8 = 40$ L.

questions.question: Angus makes 96 litres of fruit punch using 24 L of orange juice, 32 L of apple juice and 40 L of pineapple juice. The cost per litre is \$2.50 for orange juice, \$3.00 for apple juice, and \$3.50 for pineapple juice. What is the total cost of making the fruit punch?
Jake surveyed 300 pupils to find out their daily commute time. The results were used to construct the box plot below. How many pupils have a commute time between 20 and 35 minutes?
questions.answer: The box plot has $Q_1 = 20$ and median $= 35$. The data between $Q_1$ and the median is $25\%$ of the pupils: $0.25 \times 300 = 75$ pupils.

questions.question: Ollie has bought a Toyota RAV4 Hybrid. The fuel consumption is 4.8 litres per 100 kilometres. Calculate the distance that the car can travel on a full tank of 50 litres. Give your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer: Distance $= \dfrac{50}{4.8} \times 100 = 1041.67 \approx 1042$ km.

questions.question: A car has a fuel consumption of 4.8 litres per 100 kilometres. Calculate the number of litres required for the car to make the journey from Sydney to Jindabyne, 458 kilometres away. Give your answer correct to the nearest litre.
questions.answer: Litres $= \dfrac{458}{100} \times 4.8 = 21.984 \approx 22$ L.

questions.question: A journey from Sydney to Jindabyne requires 22 litres of fuel. Calculate the fuel cost for the journey, based on a price of \$1.91 per litre.
questions.answer: $22 \times 1.91 = \$42.02$ (or $21.984 \times 1.91 = \$41.99$ using the unrounded amount).

questions.question: Tom purchases a gaming console for \$850, using a credit card with no annual fee. The interest rate of 18% per annum is compounded daily on the amount owing. The full amount owing was repaid 15 days later. Calculate the amount of interest charged on the purchase, assuming that interest is charged for the 15 days. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
Amount owing after 15 days $= 850\left(1 + \dfrac{0.18}{365}\right)^{15} = \$856.31$.

Interest $= 856.31 - 850 = \$6.31$.

questions.question: Young's rule is a formula used to calculate a child's medication dosage based on age: $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, where $D$ is the child's dosage, $y$ is the age of the child in years and $A$ is the adult dosage. Cohen is 6 years old and needs some amoxicillin, where the adult dosage is 500 mg. What should Cohen's dosage be? Give your answer correct to the nearest mg.
questions.answer: $D = \dfrac{6 \times 500}{6 + 12} = 166.7 \approx 167$ mg.

questions.question: Using Young's rule $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, the correct dosage of loratadine for an 8 year old is 4 mg. What is the adult dosage? Give your answer correct to the nearest mg.
questions.answer: $4 = \dfrac{8A}{8 + 12} = \dfrac{8A}{20} \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{4 \times 20}{8} = 10$ mg.

questions.question: According to Young's rule $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, if a child's dosage was $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of an adult dosage, what age would the child be?
questions.answer:
Let $A = 2$ and $D = 1$: $1 = \dfrac{2y}{y + 12} \Rightarrow y + 12 = 2y \Rightarrow y = 12$.

The child would be 12 years old.

questions.question:
The table shows the income tax rates for Australian residents for the 2024–25 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax payable |
|---|---|
| \$0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4 288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000 |

The Medicare levy is calculated as 2% of taxable income. William paid a Medicare levy of \$2037.80 in the 2024–25 financial year. Calculate the amount of tax payable on William's taxable income, excluding the Medicare levy.
William's taxable income was \$101 890 and he had allowable deductions of \$3213. What was his gross income?
questions.answer: Gross income $=$ taxable income $+$ deductions $= 101\,890 + 3213 = \$105\,103$.

questions.question: Charlie is a courier for a logistics company which manages deliveries between several tech hubs. The diagram shows the network of offices and the travel times between them in minutes. Draw a minimum spanning tree for this network on the vertices $A$ (Atlas HQ), $B$ (Brightworks), $C$ (CloudNine), $D$ (DigiCore), $E$ (Echo Systems), $F$ (FlexNet), $G$ (GridPoint).
questions.answer: Choose edges in increasing order of weight, skipping any that form a cycle: $EF = 5$, $EG = 6$, $CE = 7$, ($CG = 8$ is skipped, it forms a cycle), $FD = 9$, ($GD = 10$ skipped), $AC = 11$, $BD = 12$. The tree is $A$–$C$, $C$–$E$, $E$–$G$, $E$–$F$, $F$–$D$, $D$–$B$.

questions.question: The minimum spanning tree for the network of tech hubs has edges of weight 11, 7, 6, 5, 9 and 12 minutes. Determine the total weight of the minimum spanning tree.

Achilles starts drinking at 2 pm. He has 5 schooners of beer over three and a half hours. Each schooner is 1.6 standard drinks, and Achilles weighs 65 kg. The formula to calculate his Blood Alcohol Content is $\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$ where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours drinking, and $M$ is the person's mass in kilograms. Calculate Achilles's Blood Alcohol Content at 5:30 pm. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

Achilles's BAC at 5:30 pm is 0.1216 (0.122 to 3 decimal places). The number of hours until his BAC returns to zero is $\text{Time to zero} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$. If Achilles consumes no more alcohol, determine at what time his Blood Alcohol Content returns to zero. Give your answer correct to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
Using the unrounded BAC: $\dfrac{0.12160633}{0.015} = 8.107$ hours $= 8$ h $6$ min after 5:30 pm, which is **1:36 am**.

(Using the rounded value $0.122$ gives $8.13$ h $= 8$ h $8$ min, which is $1{:}38$ am; the school's key accepts both.)

questions.question:
One summer, Jonah gets a job selling ice creams. Each day, he records the number of ice creams sold and the temperature.

| Temp (°C) | 26 | 27 | 29 | 30 | 32 | 33 | 34 | 37 | 39 | 40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales (units) | 162 | 172 | 200 | 202 | 253 | 250 | 274 | 311 | 291 | 353 |

Draw the last two points on the scatterplot and add a line of best fit, by eye, on the graph below.
questions.answer: Plot $(39, 291)$ and $(40, 353)$. A line of best fit by eye runs from near the bottom left (for example through $(26, 165)$) up through the middle of the points to about $(40, 340)$.

questions.question:
Using Jonah's data (temperature in °C and ice cream sales in units), write the equation of the least-squares regression line, giving your values correct to two decimal places.

| Temp (°C) | 26 | 27 | 29 | 30 | 32 | 33 | 34 | 37 | 39 | 40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales (units) | 162 | 172 | 200 | 202 | 253 | 250 | 274 | 311 | 291 | 353 |
Using Jonah's data on temperature and ice cream sales (10 days), calculate the value of Pearson's correlation coefficient, $r$. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer: $r = 0.9710\ldots \approx 0.97$.

questions.question: Pearson's correlation coefficient for Jonah's ice cream sales and the temperature is $r = 0.97$. Comment on the strength of the correlation within the context of this question.
questions.answer: There is a strong positive correlation between sales and temperature: the higher the temperature, the more ice creams are sold.

questions.question: Daniel is a conservationist. He estimates the number of wombats in a reserve using the capture-recapture method. In the first capture, 80 wombats are caught, tagged, and released. A week later, a second capture of 100 wombats is made, and 20 of them are found to be tagged. Estimate the total number of wombats in the reserve.
questions.answer: Let $x$ be the total population. The proportion tagged is the same in the sample and the population: $\dfrac{80}{x} = \dfrac{20}{100} \Rightarrow x = 80 \times \dfrac{100}{20} = 400$ wombats.

questions.question: Daniel estimates the number of wombats in a reserve using the capture-recapture method. Explain one assumption that must be made for this estimate to be valid.
questions.answer: Either: the capture is random, so every wombat has an equal chance of being selected; or the reserve is a closed population, so wombats cannot enter or leave (and none are born or die) between the two captures.

questions.question:
Angus records the number of minutes he spends exercising each day for two weeks. The stem-and-leaf plot shows the results (Key: $2 \mid 3 = 23$ minutes).

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 2 | 3 5 8 |
| 3 | 0 2 2 4 7 |
| 4 | 1 5 9 |
| 5 | 0 |
| 6 | |
| 7 | 5 |

Is 75 minutes an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
There are 13 values. The median is the 7th value, $34$. $Q_1 = \dfrac{28 + 30}{2} = 29$ and $Q_3 = \dfrac{45 + 49}{2} = 47$, so $\text{IQR} = 47 - 29 = 18$.

$Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 47 + 27 = 74$. Since $75 > 74$, 75 minutes is an outlier.

questions.question: Angus's exercise times (in minutes) are 23, 25, 28, 30, 32, 32, 34, 37, 41, 45, 49, 50, 75. Calculate the standard deviation. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer: Using the population standard deviation on a calculator, $\sigma = 13.40$ minutes.

questions.question: Angus's exercise times include an outlier at 75 minutes. Which is the better measure of spread for this data set, the interquartile range (IQR) or the standard deviation? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: The IQR is the better measure of spread because it is not affected by outliers, while the standard deviation is inflated by the outlier of 75 minutes.

questions.question: Cohen has a bag containing 4 red and 6 black marbles. Two marbles are selected at random without replacement. A partially completed tree diagram is shown below (the branch from black to black is already marked $\frac{5}{9}$). Complete the tree diagram by including the missing probabilities. Calculate the probability of choosing at least 1 black marble.
questions.answer:
First marble: $P(R) = \frac{4}{10}$, $P(B) = \frac{6}{10}$. Second marble: after R, $P(R) = \frac{3}{9}$, $P(B) = \frac{6}{9}$; after B, $P(R) = \frac{4}{9}$, $P(B) = \frac{5}{9}$.

$$P(\text{at least 1 black}) = 1 - P(\text{no black}) = 1 - \frac{4}{10} \times \frac{3}{9} = 1 - \frac{2}{15} = \frac{13}{15}$$

questions.question: Ollie installs an electric water heater. The heater uses 4.5 kWh of electricity per day. Electricity costs 30 cents per kWh. How much does it cost to run the water heater for one year? Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.

Running an electric water heater costs \$492.75 per year. Ollie considers switching to a solar water heater that costs \$1800 upfront and uses no electricity from the grid. How many years will it take to recover the cost of switching to solar?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{1800}{492.75} = 3.65$ years, so it will take **4 years** to recover the cost.

questions.question: The diagram shows one side of an irregularly shaped dam. The width of the dam is measured at 5-metre intervals (the heights are 4 m, 5 m and 2 m). Use two applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the dam.
questions.answer: $$A \approx \frac{5}{2}\left(4 + 2 \times 5 + 2\right) = \frac{5}{2}(16) = 40\ \text{m}^2$$

questions.question: The time $T$ (in hours) it takes to paint a big fence varies inversely with the number of workers $W$ painting. If it takes 4 workers 3 hours to paint the fence, how long would it take 6 workers?
questions.answer:
$T = \dfrac{k}{W}$, so $k = WT = 4 \times 3 = 12$ and $T = \dfrac{12}{W}$.

With $6$ workers: $T = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2$ hours.

questions.question: The time $T$ (in hours) it takes to paint a big fence varies inversely with the number of workers $W$, with $T = \dfrac{12}{W}$. If the fence was painted in 30 minutes, how many workers were painting the fence?
questions.answer: $0.5 = \dfrac{12}{W} \Rightarrow W = 24$ workers.

questions.question: Find the capacity of Cut 1 shown in the network flow diagram below.
questions.answer: Add the capacities of the edges that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side. Those edges have capacities $5$, $3$ and $3$. The two edges that cross the cut towards the source (the $5$ at the top and the $7$ in the lower half) are not counted. Capacity $= 5 + 3 + 3 = 11$.

questions.question:
The table shows the future value for an annuity of \$1 for varying interest rates and time periods.

| Periods ($n$) | 0.25% | 0.5% | 0.75% | 1% | 1.5% | 2% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 12.16 | 12.30 | 12.49 | 12.68 | 13.05 | 13.43 |
| 24 | 24.47 | 24.87 | 25.35 | 25.84 | 26.88 | 27.92 |
| 36 | 36.91 | 37.57 | 38.48 | 39.39 | 41.01 | 42.63 |
| 48 | 49.47 | 50.39 | 51.56 | 52.94 | 55.34 | 57.74 |
| 60 | 62.15 | 63.33 | 64.66 | 66.51 | 69.67 | 73.36 |
| 72 | 74.95 | 76.39 | 77.88 | 80.10 | 83.99 | 89.51 |

William invests \$200 at the start of each month for 5 years at 6% per annum, compounded monthly. Calculate the future value of William's investment using the table above.
questions.answer:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12} = 0.5\%$ and there are $5 \times 12 = 60$ periods. From the table, the factor is $63.33$.

$FV = 200 \times 63.33 = \$12\,666$.

questions.question: Using the annuity table of future value factors, Charlie is planning to buy a motorbike and wants to save \$5000. How much should he invest each month, in order to save \$5000 after 4 years at 9% per annum, compounded monthly?
questions.answer:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{9\%}{12} = 0.75\%$ and there are $4 \times 12 = 48$ periods. From the table, the factor is $51.56$.

$$x = \frac{5000}{51.56} = \$96.97$$

questions.question: Jake always records the time he takes to run 10 km. His times follow a normal distribution, with a mean of 52 minutes and a standard deviation of 4 minutes. What is the probability that Jake completes the run between 48 and 60 minutes?

Jake's 10 km run times are normally distributed with a mean of 52 minutes and a standard deviation of 4 minutes. On his birthday, Jake runs so well that his time is among the best 2.5% of all his recorded 10 km runs. What time separates the best 2.5% of Jake's runs from the rest?
questions.answer:
The fastest $2.5\%$ of times are those more than $2$ standard deviations below the mean (the empirical rule leaves $2.5\%$ in each tail beyond $z = \pm 2$).

$52 - 2 \times 4 = 44$ minutes.

questions.question: The diagram shows a water storage tank and its cross-section. The cross-section is a semicircle of radius 3 m with another, smaller, semicircle of radius 1.5 m cut out. What is the shaded area? Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

The water storage tank has a cross-sectional area of $10.6\ \text{m}^2$ and a capacity of 100 000 litres. Calculate the height, $x$, of the tank in metres. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer: $100\,000\ \text{L} = 100\ \text{m}^3$. Volume $=$ area $\times$ height, so $x = \dfrac{100}{10.6} = 9.43\ldots \approx 9.4$ m.

questions.question: The tank holds 100 000 litres and is connected to an irrigation system that uses water at a rate of 750 litres per hour. For how many hours and minutes can the irrigation system be used before a full tank is emptied?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{100\,000}{750} = 133.\overline{3}$ hours $= 133$ hours $20$ minutes.

questions.question: Tom is a surveyor. He stands at a fixed point $O$ and records the position of three boundary markers using bearings and distances: $P$ is 12 m from $O$ on a bearing of 020°, $Q$ is 9 m from $O$ on a bearing of 120°, and $R$ is 15 m from $O$ on a bearing of 240°. Find the area of $\triangle POQ$. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
$\angle POQ = 120^\circ - 20^\circ = 100^\circ$.

$A = \tfrac{1}{2}(12)(9)\sin 100^\circ = 53.2\ \text{m}^2$.

questions.question: Tom is a surveyor standing at $O$. $Q$ is 9 m from $O$ on a bearing of 120° and $R$ is 15 m from $O$ on a bearing of 240°. Find the bearing of $Q$ from $R$.
questions.answer:
$\angle QOR = 240^\circ - 120^\circ = 120^\circ$.

Cosine rule: $QR^2 = 9^2 + 15^2 - 2(9)(15)\cos 120^\circ = 441 \Rightarrow QR = 21$ m.

Sine rule: $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{9} = \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{21} \Rightarrow \theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9\sin 120^\circ}{21}\right) = 21.8^\circ$, where $\theta = \angle ORQ$.

$R$ is at $240^\circ$ from $O$, so $O$ is on a bearing of $240^\circ - 180^\circ = 060^\circ$ from $R$ (that is, $\angle NRO = 60^\circ$). $Q$ lies a further $21.8^\circ$ clockwise from $O$, so the bearing of $Q$ from $R$ is $60^\circ + 21.8^\circ = 081.8^\circ \approx 082^\circ$ T.
